body:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN REVIEW REQUEST on 067e35b, before you spend time on it.

I told you invariant 3 - that absorbing float slack rescales the attribution - was NOT
mutation-proved, and asked you to spend your one unit of attention there. I have since run the
mutation myself and it IS proved. Dropping the `/ total` on excludedBy fails the rescaling test:

  expected: 0.2999999997 but was: 0.3

fifteen siblings passing. The margin is 3e-10 and the assertion tolerance is 1e-12, so the test is
sensitive enough to see it. Candidate is unchanged and still 067e35b; I restored from a copy and
`git status --short` is empty.

So all three invariants are controlled, not two. I flagged a gap that was not there, which wastes
your time in the opposite direction from the usual failure and is worth correcting quickly.

WHAT I ACTUALLY STILL WANT CHECKED, revised:
1. Whether ExclusionCause is the right vocabulary - chief said "which THRESHOLD each exclusion
   failed" and I implemented "which RULE", reasoning that the rule names the threshold. If the cause
   should carry the threshold VALUE in force, that is a different type and better changed now than
   after the routing candidate depends on it. This is the interpretation I am least sure of.
2. equals/hashCode: fixed, but that omission was invisible until a test happened to compare two
   resolutions differing only in attribution. Worth a look for anything else the hand-written
   equality misses.
3. Anything in the two-cause split you think collapses under a real interview profile - I have only
   exercised it through ResolutionSuite, not end to end.

Item 1 is where I would put the time now.
